narrative-blueprint.title: Narrative Blueprint Workspace
narrative-blueprint.northStar: 仍在运行的播出线路蓝图
narrative-blueprint.overview: A local authoring instrument that translates the abandoned-station world into a dense, measurable control workspace. It is operational tooling rather than an in-fiction player surface, and its cyan, amber, grid, and editing controls remain scoped to the blueprint.

control.purpose: Buttons, graph copy, statuses, and connection labels.

field.purpose: Search, inspector inputs, and editable prose.

metadata.purpose: Field labels, node types, chapter labels, and counts.

layout.desktop: 58px top bar; 226px chapter rail; flexible canvas; 320px inspector.
layout.intermediate: At 1050px and below: 200px chapter rail beside canvas; 260px inspector below.
layout.compact: Below 700px: 48px top bar; primary canvas; 276px lower inspector; chapter selector moves into toolbar.
layout.world: 4000px by 2400px; 20px minor and 80px major grid; 10px drag snapping.

rules.name: The Canvas Owns the Workspace Rule
rules.body: Keep the graph as the dominant authoring surface at every width; navigation and inspection may relocate, but must not cover it with modal workflows.

rules.name: The Redundancy Before Color Rule
rules.body: Every node type must retain its text label and structural marker in addition to hue.

rules.name: The Blueprint Is Not the Broadcast Rule
rules.body: Reuse the game's square equipment language and two-font hierarchy, but keep authoring cyan, amber, grid lines, and dense editing controls scoped to this workspace.

dos: Do keep the graph as the first-read authoring surface.
Do pair every node hue with a label and structural distinction.
Do preserve all five file actions as icons in compact layouts.
Do use inline stroke SVGs for authoring controls.
donts: Don't apply blueprint cyan, amber, or grid styling to the player's livestream.
Don't replace node-type structure with color alone.
Don't add shadows or rounded cards to the flat authoring workspace.
Don't hide persistence or destructive state behind unlabeled desktop controls.

components.css: .ds-inspector-field{display:grid;gap:7px;width:260px;font-family:"Microsoft YaHei","PingFang SC",sans-serif}.ds-inspector-field span{color:#8f968f;font-size:9px;letter-spacing:.11em}.ds-inspector-field input{width:100%;height:34px;padding:0 9px;border:1px solid #27343c;border-radius:0;outline:0;background:#070b0e;color:#d7d8d0;font-size:11px}.ds-inspector-field input:hover{border-color:#43525a}.ds-inspector-field input:focus{border-color:#60a7b2}.ds-inspector-field input:focus-visible{outline:2px solid #edbb64;outline-offset:2px}

narrative.northStar: 最后在线的应急播出终端
narrative.overview:
The interface behaves as equipment left running inside an abandoned local television station, not as a modern streaming product. Live imagery remains the dominant material; identity, status, comments, subtitles, and interaction controls are sparse broadcast annotations laid directly over it.

The atmosphere is coal-dark, low-saturation, quiet, and operational. Faded green suggests aging phosphor and institutional equipment, while warning red is reserved for live, send, progress, and fault-bearing signals. Controls resemble old subtitle-machine fields and signal markings through square corners, hairline borders, compact labels, and restrained movement.
keyCharacteristics: Full-viewport 16:9 live image with no conventional player chrome.
Square, low-gloss controls anchored to the broadcast edges.
WenKai narrative voice paired with compact system sans-serif telemetry.
Phosphor green for station identity and warning red for consequential state.
Scanlines, edge falloff, and deep overlays integrated with the footage.

rules.name: The Signal Rarity Rule
rules.body: Warning red communicates a live, transmitting, progressing, or failed system state; it is never general decoration.

rules.name: The Image Owns the Screen Rule
rules.body: Overlay colors must preserve the live image as the first-read surface, using falloff and localized panels only where legibility requires them.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: WenKai belongs to the broadcast's human and narrative voice; sans-serif belongs to the terminal, audience, and controls.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: Do not place ornamental eyebrow text above titles; identity and state labels must perform an actual broadcast function.

rules.name: The Edge-Anchored Rule
rules.body: Reusable broadcast information attaches to the top, right safe area, or bottom edge; avoid floating task cards in the center of live footage.

rules.name: The Structural Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows separate equipment layers or restore text legibility; they do not make controls look glossy or card-like.

rules.name: The Square Console Rule
rules.body: Interactive and informational surfaces use square corners; circles are reserved for signal lamps and compact numeric attention markers.

dos: Do preserve the live image as the first viewport and anchor interaction to its bottom edge.
Do use warning red only when a broadcast action or state has consequence.
Do keep waiting, generation, failure, and recovery language inside the fiction of a relay signal.
Do maintain strong text shadows or localized dark backing where copy crosses moving footage.
Do keep self-hosted WenKai for display and narrative roles and system sans-serif for terminal roles.
donts: Don't add conventional playback controls, seek handles, task cards, modal dialogs, or dashboard navigation.
Don't round console fields and panels or apply glossy, soft-card styling.
Don't add decorative eyebrows, badges, or labels that do not communicate station identity or live state.
Don't use warning red as ambient decoration or let overlays compete with the footage.
Don't introduce anime, cel-shaded, glossy 3D, or arbitrary third-person visual language into the broadcast surface.
